items.descriptionEn: This exercise requires a sturdy box or a chair. Simple stand ~6 inches in front of it and balance yourself on one leg. From here, begin squatting down in a smooth controlled motion while keeping your other leg straight out in front of you for balance. Slowly sit down on the box, pause for a 1 count and push back up with the working leg, while never letting your other leg touch the ground.
items.author: jesusd

items.descriptionEn: Attach a D-Handle to a high pully. And use your lat muscles to pull the weight single handedly.
items.author: Expenses7000

items.descriptionEn: Begin in a half kneeling position with the leg away from the wall stabilized against the wall with a ball. With both hands directly in front of you, rotate one arm open attempting to reach the wall behind you. Exhale as you rotate, inhale as you return to neutral and repeat.
items.author: amwang4

items.descriptionEn: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, the kettlebell on the floor about 20-30 cm in front of your toes. Hinge at the hips with a slight bend in the knees and a flat back, and grip the handle with both hands. Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, then drive your hips forward explosively so that it swings forward and up to chest or shoulder height (Russian style, not overhead). Your arms stay straight and relaxed, the power comes from the hips. Let the kettlebell swing back down, hinge again as it passes between your legs and go straight into the next rep.
items.author: deusinvictus

items.descriptionEn: This is especially for the gym80 device 3008 Abdominal Crunch.
As a warmup, use light dumbbells, one in each hand. Lunge in alternating directions, forward, sideways, backwards and 45 degree angles.
items.author: philip

items.descriptionEn: Starting position: Stand straight, feet hip-width apart. Steps: Squat low and support yourself on the floor with your hands between the knees and in front of your feet, your back straight. Keeping your hands on the floor, jump your legs backward into high plank position. Jump your feet forward to return to the squat position. Repeat.
items.descriptionZh: 起始姿势：站直，双脚分开与臀部同宽。 步骤： 深蹲蹲下，双手放在膝盖之间脚前，支撑在地板上；背部挺直。 双手放在地板上，双腿向后跳到高平板支撑的位置。 双脚向前跳，回到下蹲位置。 重复。

items.descriptionEn: Dumbbell raise at an angle halfway between a front raise and a lateral raise.
Controlled breathing drill performed in a 90/90 position to encourage rib, abdominal, and pelvic coordination.
Custom description created by the Integrated Conditioning routine importer for wger.

Sit on the floor with one leg bent at 90 degrees in front of you and the other leg bent at 90 degrees out to the side, so that the rear shin is parallel to the front shin. Keep your torso upright and, if possible, your hands off the floor. Rotate both knees over to the other side so that the legs swap positions and you arrive in the same 90/90 position facing the opposite way. Move slowly and under control, keeping the feet in contact with the floor, and alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions. Mobility drill for internal and external rotation of the hips.

Starting Position : Kneel on the floor with the ab wheel in front of you. Grip the Wheel : Hold the handles firmly. Roll Out : Slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your body while keeping your core tight. Return : Pull the wheel back towards your knees, maintaining tension in your core.
items.author: lhegedus

items.descriptionEn: The Abdominal Crunch is a classic core isolation exercise performed on the floor or a mat. Unlike a full sit-up, it involves a smaller range of motion where you only lift your shoulders and upper back off the ground, keeping your lower back pressed firmly against the floor.
items.author: amaesc

items.descriptionEn: Lie on your back with knees bent. Gently pull your belly button toward your spine without moving your hips or holding your breath.
items.author: beagle

items.descriptionEn: Training a stable stance, predominantly on one leg, is crucial for both sides. On the one hand, it prevents discomfort and, on the other, it establishes a stable foundation. The practitioner assumes the usual standing position and, with a stable upper body, attempts to repeatedly lift the unloaded leg, bend it at the hip and knee, and then lower it again. The movement is also repeated on the other side. The exercise trains the stability of the hip-surrounding muscles.
items.author: tregga

items.descriptionEn: A static hold from a pull-up bar with straight elbows and actively depressed, stabilized shoulders. Grip a secure bar and let your body hang under control. Keep your elbows straight and gently draw your shoulders down, away from your ears. Maintain this active shoulder position without pulling up, swinging, or repeatedly moving the shoulder blades. Hold for up to 30 seconds. Stop earlier if your grip opens, shoulder control deteriorates, or pain occurs. Record actual seconds, grip, and any assistance used. This is distinct from a relaxed passive dead hang or a moving scapular pull-up.
items.author: nalhilal

items.descriptionEn: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Extend one leg straight out to the side with the foot flat on the floor and the toes pointing forward. Keep your back flat and slowly push your hips back towards the heel of the kneeling leg until you feel a stretch along the inside of the extended leg. Pause briefly, then return to the starting position. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching legs. Mobility exercise for the adductors and the hips.
The posterior muscles of the buttocks, hamstrings, soleus and gastrocnemius are trained more
items.author: clafal

items.descriptionEn: 1m30s of walking (~4.5 km/h) to 30 s of jog (7 km/h) and repeat
items.author: Mamo2604

items.descriptionEn: Starting position: Start standing up with dumbbells in each hand, your back straight and feet hip-width apart. Your arms should be relaxed, pointing down. Your knees should be slightly bent, your abs contracted, and your shoulders down. Steps: Bend one arm at the elbow, bringing the dumbbell up to your shoulder. Your upper arm should remain motionless during this movement. Bring the dumbbell back down until your arm is in its original relaxed position. Repeat, switching arms.

Hold two dumbbells, the arms are streched, the hands are on your side, the palms face inwards. Bend one arm at a time and bring the weight with a fast movement up. At the same time, rotate your arms by 90 degrees at the very beginning of the movement. At the highest point, rotate a little the weights further outwards. Without a pause, bring the arm back down, slowly, and do the same with the other arm. Don't allow your body to swing during the exercise, all work is done by the biceps, which are the only mucles that should move (pay attention to the elbows).
items.author: Franpol

Stand with your knees slightly bent and your back straight. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, using a neutral grip at your sides.
items.author: Mariano_O

items.descriptionEn: Start by putting the attachment in a high position on the cable station and step back about 1m from the attachment. Grab the cable pulley handle in your left hand at about head height with your elbow slightly bent. Step back with your left foot. Pull your elbow joint in toward the torso twisting slightly and perform a single-arm row. Engage the lats as you twist. Return to the starting position with cable pulley and left foot and grab the cable pulley handle in the right hand. Repeat this motion on the opposite side with your right foot stepped back.

items.descriptionEn: Slightly bent down and knees to mimic a gorilla position and pull/row up the DBs to the chest. DB stay straight (thumbs pointing up)

items.descriptionEn: Move your knee forward, keeping your heel on the ground. Hold the position for a couple of seconds and return to the starting position.

items.descriptionEn: Sit on the floor and lift one foot off the ground, for example by resting that leg on the other knee. Slowly draw circles with your foot, moving only at the ankle. Do several circles in both directions, then switch feet.

items.descriptionEn: Take all your weight onto one leg and you're going to maintain that position, keeping your hips and pelvis level the whole time. With your back in a neutral position you want to tilt yourself forward kicking your leg back up and then slowly with your glutes bring yourself back up to neutral.

items.descriptionEn: An archer pull-up is an advanced bodyweight exercise that strengthens your back and biceps, serving as a progression towards a one-arm pull-up. It gets its name from the "bow-drawing" position your body takes at the top.Here's how to do it: Grip: Grasp a pull-up bar with a wider-than-shoulder-width overhand grip. Starting Position: Hang with arms fully extended, engaging your core and keeping your shoulder blades pulled down. The Pull: Pull your body up towards one hand, similar to a regular pull-up. At the same time, extend the other arm out to the side, keeping it as straight as possible. Your chin should come towards the hand that is pulling. Hold & Lower: Briefly hold the top position where one arm is bent and pulling, and the other is extended. Slowly lower yourself back to the starting position with control. Alternate: Repeat the movement, pulling up towards the opposite hand.The key to this exercise is to keep the assisting arm as straight as possible to maximise the load on the working arm. This makes it a challenging but effective exercise for unilateral pulling strength.
